clue.text: Animals of the stage

parts.note: the stage is the stagecoach route, not the theatre: the animals are the beasts that pulled the coach between staging posts

explanation.definitionFit: Post-horses were kept at inns along a coaching route and hired to draw the stagecoach for each stage.

clue.text: Mandarin of Philadelphian mockery?

definitions.meaning: a mandarin is a small citrus fruit
the shrub Philadelphus is called mock ..., so the fruit it mocks is named

explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a kind of citrus fruit, and the Philadelphus shrub is called mock orange for its scented white blossom.

clue.text: Strange turf fate of the hypocrite

indicators.note: strange tells us the letters are made odd, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A peculiar destiny awaits the two-faced man on the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: TURF FATE rearranged gives the title character of Molière's play, a religious hypocrite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartuffe is the pious fraud of Molière's comedy, whose name became a byword for a sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Lethe's equivalent they say

parts.note: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness, so it stands for out of mind, and the proverb says another state amounts to the same thing

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'out of sight, out of mind' makes not being seen equal to being forgotten, which is what the river Lethe brings.

clue.text: Triste, that's flat, my dashing darling

parts.note: triste is French for sad
the folk song 'Dashing Away with the Smoothing Iron' has the singer watching his darling dashing away with her smoothing tool for pressing clothes

explanation.surface: A melancholy lover sighs that his spirited sweetheart has gone cold on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The refrain of the English folk song 'Dashing Away with the Smoothing Iron' supplies the IRON; a sad-iron is a heavy flatiron, so 'flat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sad-iron is a solid heavy flatiron heated on the stove for pressing clothes.

clue.text: A legendary story takes city, to wit

indicators.note: takes here means takes away, so the word for city is subtracted from the word for wit

parts.note: wit in the sense of wisdom, shrewdness, sagacity
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old tale captures a whole town, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as the answer plus CITY makes wit: SAGA + CITY = SAGACITY. 'to wit' looks like 'namely' but here means 'to give wit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is an Old Norse prose narrative of heroic legend, and by extension any long story.

clue.text: Sound of a bell — stopping this fight ?

definitions.meaning: the two-note ringing noise a bell makes
a hammer-and-tongs fight, and a boxing round ends at the bell

explanation.definitionFit: The ringing of a bell is imitated as ding-dong, and a fiercely contested fight is called a ding-dong battle, which in boxing the bell interrupts.

clue.text: Ram-jet ? Notoriously unsatisfactory

definitions.meaning: a ram that is jet in colour, a dark male ovine
the disgraced member of a family

explanation.definitionFit: A jet ram is a dark male of the flock, and the disgraced member of a family is likened to the one dark animal among white ones.

clue.text: Whereby " the isle is full of noises "today

definitions.text: Whereby " the isle is full of noises "today

parts.words: Whereby " the isle is full of noises "today
parts.note: in The Tempest the spirit Ariel fills Prospero's island with music; today the noises come in through a wireless set's receiving wire, whose name sounds like the spirit's

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Tempest asked what fills the enchanted island with sound in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Caliban's 'the isle is full of noises' from The Tempest, where the spirit Ariel makes the music; the modern radio wire that brings in sound has a name pronounced like that spirit's.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio receives broadcasts through a wire or rod antenna, the device that fills a modern home with voices and music.

clue.text: " Catherine love Edward "" cried Poll

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out a declaration of love between Catherine and Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Poll is the stock name for a pet parrot, so 'cried Poll' means repeated words mechanically, the way a parrot does.
explanation.definitionFit: Poll is the traditional name for a pet parrot, and what it cried it repeated by rote.

clue.text: Is eager "I see" in letters for an introduction

parts.note: taken as written
agog means eagerly expectant

indicators.note: said as letters of the alphabet, the two words come out as the names of two letters

parts.note: the phrase spoken is the names of the letters I and C

explanation.surface: Someone keen exclaims that they understand, writing it in a letter of introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in letters' means the spoken words are written as the two letters whose names they sound like: I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: An isagogic work is introductory, especially one introducing the study of scripture.

clue.text: What a breaker this slavey sounds to have been !

indicators.note: sounds says the word for the breaker is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: a breaker is a wave crashing on the shore, surf

explanation.surface: Someone muses on what a household skivvy who breaks things might have been called.
explanation.walkthrough: A breaker is a wave, not a clumsy servant; slavey is old slang for a maid of all work.
explanation.definitionFit: A slavey is a drudge of a servant, and the medieval bondsman tied to the land was the original drudge.

clue.text: Piquant quality that goes to the making of a jumper?

definitions.text: Piquant quality that goes to the making of a jumper?

parts.words: Piquant quality that goes to the making of a jumper
parts.note: salt gives piquancy, and the word that starts with it describes a creature that moves by leaps, such as a jumping spider

explanation.definitionFit: Saltigrade means moving by leaps, from Latin saltus, a leap, as with jumping spiders.

clue.text: Gordian adjuncts ?

parts.note: Alexander cut the Gordian knot with his blade, so the knots attached to blades are playfully called Gordian

explanation.definitionFit: A sword-knot is a tassel or loop of ribbon tied to a sword hilt, an attachment to the weapon that cut the famous knot.

clue.text: Where Dan Leno first learned his art of pantomime ?

definitions.text: Where Dan Leno first learned his art of pantomime ?

parts.words: Where Dan Leno first learned his art of pantomime
parts.note: Dan Leno was the famous Victorian comedian in drag roles as the pantomime lady, so his training is pictured as a school for that role

explanation.definitionFit: A dame school was a small elementary school run by an old woman, and in British pantomime the dame is the comic woman played by a man, Dan Leno's speciality.

clue.text: The wrinkle time induces in all our old 'uns

parts.note: a wrinkle is a line on the skin
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time etches wrinkles on all our elderly relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, the whole line of forebears from whom a family descends.

clue.text: No archdeacon is seen on a railway's termini about nine

parts.note: taken as written
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
the outside letters of the word railway, its first and last, are R and Y

explanation.surface: A railway terminus has no archdeacon in sight at around nine o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Novenary means relating to the number nine or consisting of nine.

clue.text: Self-satisfied with a leg-break -run!

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied

indicators.note: break tells us the letters of the word leg are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cocky cricketer bowls a leg-break and shouts for the batsmen to run.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg-break is a cricket delivery that spins from the leg side; here 'break' rearranges LEG into GLE. 'Run' means carry contraband, as in gun-running.
explanation.definitionFit: To run goods is to carry them in secretly past customs, as rum-runners and gun-runners do.

clue.text: The flowers for classical! garden fencing?

definitions.text: The flowers for classical! garden fencing?

parts.words: The flowers for classical! garden fencing
parts.note: the classical Latin plural of the flower's name, which means little swords, so a bed of them is swordplay in the garden

explanation.definitionFit: Gladiolus means little sword in Latin, from the blade-shaped leaves, and its classical plural ends in -i.

clue.text: The gods he swore by were 16

definitions.text: The gods he swore by were 16

parts.words: The gods he swore by were 16
parts.note: Macaulay's Horatius opens with a king of Clusium who swore by the nine gods, the number given by entry 16

explanation.definitionFit: Lars Porsena of Clusium, in Macaulay's Lays of Ancient Rome, 'by the Nine Gods he swore'.

clue.text: Many a volume of Kipling's

parts.note: Kipling published a short-story collection whose title starts with the word Many; the solver supplies the rest of the title

explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling's 1893 collection of stories is titled Many Inventions.

clue.text: Where's the anaesthetist-or weathercock ?

definitions.meaning: the anaesthetist is at the operation
a weathercock sits on the very top of a spire

explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'at op' it says where an anaesthetist works, at an operation; as one word it means perched on top, like a weathercock on a steeple.

clue.text: Stonecrop, otherwise conifer

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, otherwise
a pine is a cone-bearing tree

explanation.surface: A rock plant listed beside a pine tree as an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine is a sedum, one of the succulent plants commonly called stonecrop.

clue.text: 17'd wines — searches for them

parts.note: clue 17 means run contraband, so the past tense of that sense is ran
sack is an old name for dry white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: Smuggled wines, and the customs men hunt high and low for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 17-across is SMUGGLE in its sense 'run', so '17'd' is RAN. Sack is the sherry-like wine Falstaff drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search it thoroughly and roughly.

clue.text: To all intents a temporary lodgement

definitions.text: To all intents a temporary lodgement

parts.words: To all intents a temporary lodgement
parts.note: read 'to all in tents': a place where everyone sleeps under canvas for a while

explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a temporary settlement, often of tents, set up for soldiers, travellers or holidaymakers.

clue.text: To make coin come somehow a business must be this

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some new order

explanation.surface: A firm has to be run so that it makes money come in.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic business is one that pays its way, run at a profit rather than a loss.

clue.text: A county girl, the egoist's lost fiancée

definitions.meaning: in George Meredith's novel The Egoist

explanation.definitionFit: Durham is a county of north-east England, and also the surname of Constantia, the fiancée who runs off from the self-absorbed hero of Meredith's The Egoist.

clue.text: The (under)world his oyster?

parts.note: turns the saying 'the world is his oyster' into someone working beneath the waves, for whom oysters really are the world

explanation.definitionFit: A pearl-diver plunges under the sea to gather oysters that may hold pearls.
